blocks.x: Our annual Readers' Choice Awards winners have been announced! We loved poring over the results to find out what’s sticking with readers and spinning the data into a snapshot of the current moment in travel. Ahead: your manual for planning that next adventure. View the complete list of Readers’ Choice Award winners here.

Walt Whitman was certainly not thinking of an airport when he wrote, “I know of nothing else but miracles,” but just as the poet finds wonder in everything from sharing a meal with friends to watching machinery at work, might he also have celebrated the unexpected beauty we sometimes find in the modern-day hellscape of an airport?

If a leaf of grass is no less than the journey-work of the stars, the art inside an airport that reminds us of our humanity and distracts us from our fatigue is an object worthy of praise. But until it’s taken up in verse, other forms of recognition will have to do, such as a dedicated category in Skytrax’s World Airline Awards. Industry insiders call the honors, “the Oscars of the aviation industry,” and its 2026 winners for “World’s Best Art in the Airport” are sure to get the discourse flowing. AV geek or average flyer, we can all be the judge of which ones swept, got snubbed, and deserve a layover in. To reveal a little of our own hand, these also happen to be some of our favorite airports. And according to our Readers’ Choice Awards, they are some of yours, too.
With no further ado, these are the winners for “World’s Best Art in the Airport,” in ranked order.

blocks.x: 1. The Houston Airport System - George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) and William P. Hobby Airport (HOU)

For the fourth year running, first place is this Texas-based twofer. Comprised of George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) and William P. Hobby Airport (HOU), the Houston Airport System and its arts program are sterling examples of the old adage that everything is bigger, and evidently better, in the Lone Star State. Case in point, take IAH’s handblown glass centerpiece, Coastal Prairie Fiori, by artist Dale Chihuly. The intricate, snaking sculpture is comprised of 537 individual elements suspended from the rafters. Or, should you find yourself at HOU, you can’t miss the David Adickes’ We Love Houston sculpture, the towering photo-op moment stands at 16.5 feet tall. In addition to the visual arts, the Houston Airports Public Art Program also includes artist residencies and their “Harmony in the Air” performances that brings in over 120 live musicians to fill the air across both airports’ terminals.

blocks.x: Changi is an airport that is no stranger to superlatives. Having snatched “World’s Best Airport” at the Skytrax World Airport Awards 14 times, it is literally the institution’s most awarded airport. As a massive 1.46 million-square-foot shopping complex complete with gold bar-vending machines and the iconic Jewel Rain Vortex, Changi is a destination onto itself. And its stunning art program is a synecdoche for the Singaporean airport as a whole, with a major theme in the curation being the marriage of nature with technology and culture. There’s Terminal 1’s Kinetic Rain sculpture, a dancing wave of 1,216 copper-plated droplets that rises and falls with perfect synchronicity, as well as Terminal 3’s affecting Coming Home statues created by artist Han Meilin which greets visitors at the South Arrival Immigration Hall, and both pieces are part of the airport's permanent collection. While Changi invites its denizens to embrace its maximalism, there’s nothing wrong with stopping to smell the sculpted roses.
